### 3.4.1 – The Basic Strategy

Up until now, the variable was always on one side of the equation. But sometimes we’ll see the variable appear on **both sides**. This adds a step to solving equations:

**Get all the variables on one side and the numbers on the other.**

Let’s use the apple-and-scale model to see how this works.

**Example 1:**

Here we have 3 apples and 1 weight on the left-hand side, and 1 apple and 7 weights on the right-hand side.

![](/images/Unit_3/Lesson_4/Balance_2a_plus_1_equal_a_plus_7.png){width="300px" fig-align="center"}

$$
3a + 1 = a + 7
$$

To find the weight of an apple, we need apples on one side and weights on the other. We start by removing an apple from the right pan.

![](/images/Unit_3/Lesson_4/Balance_2a_plus_1_equal_a_plus_7_2.png){width="300px" fig-align="center"}

$$
\begin{align*}
3a + 1 &= a + 7 \textcolor{red}{- a} \\
3a + 1 &\neq 7
\end{align*}
$$

The scale lost its balance! Always remember to **do the same thing to both sides** of the equation!

![](/images/Unit_3/Lesson_4/Balance_2a_plus_1_equal_a_plus_7_3.png){width="300px" fig-align="center"}

$$
\begin{align*}
3a + 1 \textcolor{red}{- a} &= a + 7 \textcolor{red}{- a} \\
2a + 1 &= 7
\end{align*}
$$

Removing an apple from **both sides** kept the balance. Now we just have a two-step equation.

Step 1: Remove a weight from both pans.

![](/images/Unit_3/Lesson_4/Balance_2a_plus_1_equal_a_plus_7_4.png){width="300px" fig-align="center"}

$$
\begin{align*}
2a + 1 \textcolor{red}{-1} &= 7 \textcolor{red}{-1} \\
2a &= 6
\end{align*}
$$

Step 2: Take half of what is in each pan.

![](/images/Unit_3/Lesson_4/Balance_2a_plus_1_equal_a_plus_7_5.png){width="300px" fig-align="center"}

$$
\begin{align*}
2a \textcolor{red}{\div 2} &= 6 \textcolor{red}{\div 2} \\
a &= 3
\end{align*}
$$

An apple has a weight of **3**.

---

**Example 2:**

Solve $4x + 5 = 2x + 9$.

$$
\begin{align*}
4x + 5 &= 2x + 9 \\
\\
4x + 5 \textcolor{red}{- 2x} &= 2x + 9 \textcolor{red}{- 2x} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{$-2x$ both sides}}} \\
2x + 5 &= 9 \\
\\
2x + 5 \textcolor{red}{- 5} &= 9 \textcolor{red}{- 5} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{-5 both sides}}} \\
2x &= 4 \\
\\
2x \textcolor{red}{\div 2} &= 4 \textcolor{red}{\div 2} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{÷2 both sides}}} \\
x &= 2
\end{align*}
$$

:::{.you-try title="Solve $5x + 3 = 2x + 12$."}
$$
\begin{align*}
5x + 3 &= 2x + 12 \\
\\
5x + 3 \textcolor{red}{- 2x} &= 2x + 12 \textcolor{red}{- 2x} \\
3x + 3 &= 12 \\
\\
3x + 3 \textcolor{red}{- 3} &= 12 \textcolor{red}{- 3} \\
3x &= 9 \\
\\
3x \textcolor{red}{\div 3} &= 9 \textcolor{red}{\div 3} \\
x &= 3
\end{align*}
$$
:::

---

### 3.4.2 – Simplifying Before Solving

Not every equation is ready to solve right away. Sometimes, each side of the equation has parentheses or extra terms that must be simplified first. The strategy is:

1. Simplify both sides (distribute, combine like terms).
2. Get all variables on the **left side**.
3. Solve as usual.

---

**Example 1:**

Solve $2(x + 3) = 3x + 1$.

$$
\begin{align*}
\textcolor{red}{2}(x + 3) &= 3x + 1 \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{Distribute the 2}}} \\
2x + 6 &= 3x + 1  \\
\\
2x + 6 \textcolor{red}{- 3x} &= 3x + 1 \textcolor{red}{- 3x} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{$-3x$ both sides}}}\\
-x + 6 &= 1 \\
\\
-x + 6 \textcolor{red}{- 6} &= 1 \textcolor{red}{- 6} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{-6 both sides}}}\\
-x &= -5 \\
\\
-x \textcolor{red}{\div -1} &= 1 \textcolor{red}{\div -1} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{÷-1 both sides}}} \\
x &= 5
\end{align*}
$$

---

**Example 2:**

Solve $4x + 5 + x = 2x + 12$.

$$
\begin{align*}
\textcolor{blue}{4x} + 6 + \textcolor{blue}{x} &= 2x + 12 \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{Combine like terms}}} \\
\textcolor{blue}{5x} + 6 &= 2x + 12  \\
\\
5x + 6 \textcolor{red}{- 2x} &= 2x + 12 \textcolor{red}{- 2x} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{$-2x$ both sides}}}\\
3x + 6 &= 12 \\
\\
3x + 6 \textcolor{red}{- 6} &= 12 \textcolor{red}{- 6} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{-6 both sides}}}\\
3x &= 6 \\
\\
3x \textcolor{red}{\div 3} &= 6 \textcolor{red}{\div 3} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{÷3 both sides}}} \\
x &= 2
\end{align*}
$$

---

**Example 3:**

Solve $3(x - 2) + 4 = 2(x + 1)$.

$$
\begin{align*}
\textcolor{red}{3}(x - 2) + 4 &= \textcolor{red}{2}(x + 1) \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{Distribute both sides}}}\\
3x - 6 + 4 &= 2x + 2  \\
\\
3x \textcolor{blue}{- 6} + \textcolor{blue}{4} &= 2x + 2 \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{Combine like terms}}} \\
3x \textcolor{blue}{- 2} &= 2x + 2 \\
\\
3x - 2 \textcolor{red}{- 2x} &= 2x + 2 \textcolor{red}{- 2x} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{$-2x$ both sides}}}\\
x - 2 &= 2 \\
\\
x - 2 \textcolor{red}{+ 2} &= 2 \textcolor{red}{+ 2} \tag*{\class{stepnote}{\textcolor{gray}{+2 both sides}}}\\
x &= 4
\end{align*}
$$

---

:::{.you-try title="Solve $2(x + 4) = x + 10$."}

$$
\begin{align*}
2(x + 4) &= x + 10 \\
\\
2x + 8 &= x + 10 \\
\\
2x + 8 \textcolor{red}{- x} &= x + 10 \textcolor{red}{- x} \\
x + 8 &= 10 \\
\\
x + 8 \textcolor{red}{- 8} &= 10 \textcolor{red}{- 8} \\
x &= 2
\end{align*}
$$

:::
